items.stem: Which of the following best describes "arc length (radians)"?

items.answer: The formula s = rθ, where θ is in radians

items.stem: Explain why y = sin x has period 360°.
items.answer: The point on the unit circle returns to the same position after a full turn, so the values repeat every 360°.

items.stem: Explain why y = tan x has period 180° rather than 360°.
items.answer: tan(x + 180°) = sin(x + 180°)/cos(x + 180°) = (−sin x)/(−cos x) = tan x.

items.answer: For cosine the second solution is 360° − 66.4° = 293.6°.

items.stem: Compare y = 4 sin x and y = sin 3x. (a) State the amplitude and period of the first. (b) State them for the second. (c) Describe each as a transformation of y = sin x. (d) Predict the features of y = 4 sin 3x.
items.answer: (a) 4 sin x: amplitude 4, period 360° (b) sin 3x: amplitude 1, period 120° (c) 4 is a vertical stretch; 3 a horizontal stretch by 1/3 (d) y = 4 sin 3x has amplitude 4 and period 120°
items.markingKey: (a) 4 sin x: amplitude 4, period 360° (b) sin 3x: amplitude 1, period 120° (c) 4 is a vertical stretch; 3 a horizontal stretch by 1/3 (d) y = 4 sin 3x has amplitude 4 and period 120°. items.stem: A pendulum in a science museum in Singapore is 0.8 m long and swings 25° each side of the vertical. (a) Find the total angle of a swing in radians. (b) Find the arc length of one swing. items.answer: (a) 50° = 0.873 rad (b) 0.698 m per swing (c) 69.8 m in 100 swings (d) the swing angle decreases because of friction

items.stem: A ferry at Mumbai needs at least 4.5 m of water. High tide (7.3 m) is at t = 0 and low tide is 2 m; the period is 12.4 hours. (a) Write a model for the depth h. (b) For how long in each cycle can the ferry enter? (c) Describe how often these windows occur. (d) Give one reason the model might be inaccurate.
items.answer: (a) h = 2.65 cos(29.03t) + 4.65 (b) 6.42 hours per cycle with h > 4.5 m (c) safe windows start every 12.4 hours (d) weather and storm surges change the tide

items.stem: The mean temperature in Halifax is modelled by T = −6 cos(30(t − 1)) + 18, t in months (t = 1 is January). (a) Write an equation for T = 21. (b) Rearrange it. (c) Solve for 1 ≤ t ≤ 13. (d) Interpret the solutions.
items.answer: (a) −6 cos(30(t − 1)) + 18 = 21 (b) cos(30(t − 1)) = −0.500 (c) t ≈ 5.00, 9.00 (d) the temperature is above 21 °C for about 4.0 months
items.markingKey: (a) −6 cos(30(t − 1)) + 18 = 21 (b) cos(30(t − 1)) = −0.500 (c) t ≈ 5.00, 9.00 (d) the temperature is above 21 °C for about 4.0 months. Equation set up (M1); principal value and symmetry used (A1 A1); all solutions in the domain (A1); interpretation (D: R1).

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The horizontal length of one complete cycle: 360°/b (or 2π/b in radians)"?
items.answer: period
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of period.

items.stem: Convert 90° to radians.
Which of the following best describes "phase shift"?
options: All solutions within a given domain, found using symmetry and the period
A = ½r²θ, where θ is in radians
The angle at the centre of a circle subtended by an arc equal in length to the radius; π radians = 180°
The horizontal translation c in y = a sin(b(t − c)) + d
items.answer: The horizontal translation c in y = a sin(b(t − c)) + d
items.markingKey: D. "phase shift" is the horizontal translation c in y = a sin(b(t − c)) + d.

items.stem: Explain why 3 sin x = 3.5 has no solutions.
items.answer: sin x = 1.17 > 1, but −1 ≤ sin x ≤ 1.
items.markingKey: Rearranged (A1); range of sine (R1).

items.stem: Jonas says y = sin 3x has period 1080°. Explain the error.
items.answer: Multiplying x by 3 makes the cycle happen 3 times as fast: period 360°/3 = 120°.
items.markingKey: Effect of b (R1); period (A1).

items.stem: Isabel writes: "s = rθ works with θ in degrees." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: θ must be in radians; in degrees use s = θ/360 × 2πr.
items.markingKey: θ must be in radians; in degrees use s = θ/360 × 2πr. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Ana models a quantity with max 27 and min 9 using amplitude 18. Explain the error.
items.answer: The amplitude is half the distance from max to min: (27 − 9)/2 = 9.
items.markingKey: Definition (R1); value (A1).

items.stem: A student claims: "The calculator answer to sin⁻¹ 0.6 is the only solution." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.markingKey: In 0°–360° there is also 180° − 36.9° = 143.1°. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why y = 5 sin x + 6 never takes negative values.
items.answer: sin x ranges from −1 to 1, so y ranges from 6 − 5 = 1 to 11; the minimum 1 is positive.
items.markingKey: Range of sin (R1); min value (A1).

items.stem: A sector of a circle of radius 19 cm has area 509 cm². Find the angle in radians and the perimeter of the sector, to 3 s.f.
items.answer: 2.82 rad; perimeter 91.6 cm
items.markingKey: θ = 2A/r² (M1) = 2.82 (A1); perimeter rθ + 2r = 91.6 cm (A1).

items.stem: The depth of water at a jetty is D = 4 cos(18t) + 12 metres, t hours after midnight. (a) Find D at t = 10. (b) For how long in each 20-hour cycle is the depth more than 13.4 m?
items.answer: (a) 8.00 m (b) about 7.7 hours

items.stem: The mean monthly temperature in Cape Town ranges from 8 °C in January (t = 1) to 28 °C in July (t = 7). (a) Find the amplitude and principal axis. (b) Find b (degrees per month). (c) Write a model using cosine. (d) Use it to estimate the temperature in month 2.

items.stem: A Ferris wheel in Valparaíso has radius 20 m and hub 22 m above the ground, with one turn every 10 minutes; you board at the bottom. (a) Write the height model.
